question: What is the percentage change in allocation for the Smart Cities Mission in India from the Revised Estimates of 2023-24 to the Budget Estimates of 2024-25?
solution:
The correct answer is **__70%__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Budget Estimates (BE) for the Smart Cities Mission in 2024-25 show a decrease of **70% compared to the Revised Estimates (RE) for 2023-24**.
 
• The Smart Cities Mission is a flagship program launched by the Government of India in **2015** to enhance urban infrastructure and development.
 
• The reduction in allocation reflects the government’s **reprioritization of urban development funding** or the nearing completion of key projects under the mission.
 
• The allocation adjustments are typically influenced by factors such as **project progress, expenditure efficiency, and broader fiscal constraints**.
 
• For 2024-25, the focus may shift toward other urban infrastructure schemes or **consolidation of ongoing Smart Cities projects**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Smart Cities Mission:**

 
 
• Launched on **25 June 2015**, the mission aims to promote sustainable and inclusive cities.
 
• It is implemented by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and has a target of **developing 100 smart cities** across the country.
 
• The focus areas include **urban mobility, sanitation, energy efficiency, digital governance, and affordable housing**.
 
 
 
• **Budget Estimates vs. Revised Estimates:**
 
 
• Budget Estimates represent the **initial allocation** for a financial year.
 
• Revised Estimates reflect adjustments based on actual spending trends and fiscal priorities during the year.
 
• Changes between BE and RE indicate the government’s **dynamic resource allocation strategy**.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Urban Development:**
 
 
• Urban areas face issues such as **overcrowding, inadequate infrastructure, pollution, and resource constraints**.
 
• Smart Cities aim to address these by leveraging **technology, innovation, and sustainable practices**.
 
 
 
• **Fiscal Management in India:**
 
 
• The government balances funding across competing priorities such as **health, education, defense, and infrastructure**.
 
• Changes in allocation reflect efforts to **optimize spending and improve project outcomes**.
